verdict.rationale: Restate splits the orchestration server (durable journal and invocation routing) from user services. Those services run in your own infrastructure as containers, serverless functions, VMs, or Kubernetes pods [restate-docs-7], and the vendor confirms it does not host user code [restate-comm-9]. Restate Cloud offers a vendor-managed server, while BYOC runs a managed Restate region inside your own cloud account so data can stay in your environment [restate-docs-14]; only Restate needs network access to your services, and request identity lets services verify calls come from your Restate instance [restate-docs-33, restate-docs-12]. Missing for 10: detailed BYOC documentation on what the vendor manages versus what stays in your account, network and connectivity requirements between the managed control plane and private workers, and independent hands-on corroboration of the BYOC model.
